Forging BLADE (, Xenoblade X Short Story - Creation of BLADE) is a short story for Xenoblade Chronicles X written by Yuichiro Takeda, one of the game's scenario writers. The original Japanese text can be found in the [http://xenobladex.jp/blade/index.html Special section] of the official website. The first part of the story describes Tatsu's ordinary life until his capture by the Ganglion. The following parts, 2 to 5, follow Nagi and the crew of the White Whale as they eke out an existence after crash-landing on the new planet, Mira. Finally, the story describes the creation of BLADE.

Runic power is the secondary resource used by death knights. Runic power builds up as the death knight use their abilities, displayed as an empty bar that fills up with a light sky blue color under the death knight's health bar. Generally, offensive rune abilities generate 10 runic power per rune required to use that ability. Additionally, Empower Rune Weapon generates runic power without costing runes. Death knights can hold a maximum 100 runic power, which can be increased with talents. As with rage, runic power gradually diminishes when not in combat.

The maps for the expeditions will be provided by the gnomes and goblins, who have developed a new technology to find which islands may contain Azerite. Ships to the islands will depart from faction hubs. Island Expeditions unlock through the War Campaign account-wide. One can then do Island Expeditions on alts as they level.

Kupp Coincare is a deceased goblin on Darkmoon Island. His ghost is located on the northern part of the island and is only visible while dead. He is one of several ghosts on the island. According to Kupp, he had a substantial amount of debt that he was not able to repay on his own. After approaching Silas Darkmoon and offering to work for the Faire, Silas would repay Kupp's debt personally. However, Kupp grew tired of working for the Faire and attempted to leave after he suspected most of his debt was repaid. He did not survive escaping the island though, instead, presumably becoming another victim of the surrounding woods.

Mage hunters are former members of the Kirin Tor that have opted to side with the blue dragonflight in the hopes of retaining power or simply in order to protect Azeroth from the use of uncontrolled magic, sharing the azure dragon's point of view. Transformed and bolstered by Malygos, they are tasked with rooting out and, if necessary, destroying magical artifacts; killing or imprisoning individuals who practice magic without Malygos' permission; and aiding in the redirection of ley lines using massive constructs called surge needles. Some of the mage hunters were not recruited voluntarily, but instead conscripted by the threat of their family being killed if they didn't join.

Here, tauren and night elves coexist peacefully, united by their reverence for the spirit of nature. Conflict between the races in Moonglade is not tolerated by the Moonglade Wardens stationed throughout the main town of Nighthaven, who will respond to any violence initiated against individuals with a favorable reputation with the Circle. The moonkin caves are a series of small caves whose entrances are bordered by rocks and guarded by humanoids called Moonkins. In the caves dwell many materials needed for quests such as the two druidic quests. In Moonkin, you must defeat a powerful Moonkin named Lunaclaw and Gathering the Cure is the last working part in a chain of quests leading to the learning of the spell Cure Poison. The caves lie directly east of Auberdine. They are surrounded by small camps of Moonkins around level 12-13.

Moonfang Dreadhowls are elite wolves that appear in the forest west of Darkmoon Faire on the Darkmoon Island, after all of the Moonfang Snarlers have been killed. A zone-wide announcement will be made when they appear. After most of them are killed, Moonfang will appear.

A rift is located beneath the Maelstrom. During the Great Sundering, as if struck by a giant hammer, Zin-Azshari and the Well of Eternity were blasted downward toward the ocean floor. The Well pierced the planet's molten core just before being utterly obliterated. As it was driven downward into the sea, the Well of Eternity continued to collapse in on itself and was finally obliterated. Its violent destruction has left behind a deep trench on the ocean floor that reaches all the way to the planet's core. To this day that core remains exposed and heats the ocean's cold waters. The magical energies that still emanate from the trench have caused monstrous mutations in all nearby living things.

Rinling is a sand troll quest giver found in Darkmoon Island. He runs the shooting gallery in the Darkmoon Faire. Rinling has to keep a smile on your face, or he has to cut off his hand and eat no flesh until it regenerates. He also likes collecting engineering parts, to improve his tent. Judging from his skin tone, he is a Sand troll. Once the Faire permanently moved to Darkmoon Island, Rinling finally had enough parts to open his shooting gallery, but he still has plenty of work to keep him busy. He not only collects more prizes to give out, but also uses his engineering skills to fix and refurbish the steam tonks.

The Sewers (or the bat sewer entrances) are a side entrance to the Undercity, accessible from west of the main gate to the Ruins of Lordaeron, near the Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades. This is used as the quickest way in and out for flight paths, as the only other way into the city is by using elevators from the ruins. The Shadowleaves are a group of night elf Sentinels led by Shandris Feathermoon. They fought alongside the demigod Cenarius with the Nightblades, Moonhunters, and Starseekers against Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan. When the Nightblades destroyed one of the Warsong bases the Shadowleaves established in the destroyed base, from which they sent periodic attacks against the Warsong clan. The Shadowmoon clan, also spelled Shadow Moon clan, was a relatively peaceful and highly spiritual and shamanistic orcish clan that dwelled in Shadowmoon Valley. Their last known chieftain, Ner'zhul, was deceived by the Burning Legion into forming the first Horde due to the manipulations of the warlock Gul'dan and his master, the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Following the Horde's defeat during the Second War, the Shadowmoon came to be the most powerful of the orcish clans remaining on Draenor when Ner'zhul rallied the scattered clans under his own banner. After Ner'zhul inadvertently ripped Draenor apart, many of the remaining Shadowmoon became fel orcs and entered the service of the Fel Horde.

Shadowmoon Village is a Horde settlement located in Shadowmoon Valley in Outland. It is defended by Kor'kron guards, the elite guards of Thrall's fortress of Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, back on Azeroth. Horde players who have reached the level of 70 are able to purchase personal flying mounts at the wyvern stables. Shadowmoon Village also has a flight path and an inn. Several scouts are locked in battle with Infernals on the outside walls. Shadowmoon Village is commanded by Overlord Or'barokh.

Shattered Sun Trainees are blood elven and draenei Shattered Sun Offensive soldiers training for the war and battles on the Isle of Quel'Danas. They can be found living and training around the Terrace of Light in Shattrath City. These trainees are training to become warriors, marksmen, clerics, magi and peacekeepers. Some go to the island as recruits and await their orders from an official in Sun's Reach. Shattered Sun Trainees are usually taught by a Shattered Sun Veteran and they are often visited by Lady Liadrin.

After the Shatterspear tribe joined the Horde, the Horde built the pass leading to their vale with palisade walls at the bottom and towers along the road leading up to the tunnel entrance. It is attacked and later, through phasing, occupied by the vengeful night elves of Darkshore whose Sentinels are seen patrolling it while troll corpses dots the ground. The Waking Shores storyline begins the Dragonflight campaign proper, taking place at the ancestral home of the red and black dragonflights. A wild, untamed land rife with elemental magic, the Waking Shores are the first zone that players see when they arrive to the Isles with a joint Explorers' League–Reliquary expedition. In the zone there are gorlocs and trolls. The zone storyline sees Alexstrasza summoning the Alliance and Horde to aid the red flight against the native Djaradin, while Wrathion seeks to reclaim the Obsidian Citadel of the black flight from enemy hands and come to terms with the state of his ruined flight.

Windward Isle, also known as Wind Cloud Serpent Island, can be found off Jade Forest's northeastern coast in the Mistveil Sea. This island is one of the few locations where wild cloud serpents have nests and lay eggs. The Order of the Cloud Serpent watches over this island protecting their kind, however, the Slitherscale saurok have begun invading the island stealing the eggs and even killing the serpents young and old. The cloud serpents mostly keep the southern part of the island, while nature sprites and tigers live in the northern section. The Slitherscale saurok have claimed the eastern side of the island where the turtles inhabit.

Whenever a damaging ability hits a caster mid-cast, the cast time will be set back by a given amount, slowing and delaying the cast. In contrast, pushback removes time from channelled abilities, causing them to end earlier. Pushback therefore reduces the speed of cast-time abilities, while reducing the mana efficiency of channeled abilities. Scribes (or inscribers) are literate professionals responsible for the writing, copying, compiling, and preserving of records. Many are also practitioners of inscription, weaving words of power into glyphs that can improve heroes' skills and abilities, and add special effects not possible by normal means. They are known to craft powerful staves, trinkets, and battle equipment. By transferring their magical powers into ink, the scribes can also create consumable scrolls, mystic tomes, Darkmoon cards, and pieces of vellum that allow enchantments to be passed between adventurers.

Faerie dragons (also known as sprites, sprite darters, blink dragons, fey dragons, fae dragons, or fey drakes) are diminutive, intelligent creatures that look like flying lizards (much like a chameleon with butterfly wings). Focus is the resource that both Hunters and their pets expend to use their respective abilities. Focus is similar to the Rogue's Energy resource, in that it is a constant 100 points (105/110 with the Hunter Exotic Beasts talent Kindred Spirits). By default the focus bar is full and when used, it regenerates fairly slowly (see below). The regeneration rate is not affected by being in combat. Many focus-using abilities have cooldowns as well, so hunters will often be concerned with maintaining enough focus to use abilities on cooldown, rather than pooling it for large focus dumps.

It was a dark and foreboding place of narrow cobblestone streets and crowded, Gothic houses, divided into four districts, centered around the Light's Dawn Cathedral. Shortly after the Cataclysm, the city was struck by a worgen assault and, later, a Forsaken invasion. After its abandonment by the Gilneans, the Alliance initially managed to retake the city, although it was ultimately left ruined and abandoned.

Gruul the Dragonkiller was the gronn overlord of the ogres of Outland, ruling with an iron fist.
